channel.title: Crypto Record
channel.description: Crypto Record reports news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, DeFi protocols, exchanges, stablecoins, regulation and network upgrades across the crypto market.

item.title: How Monero Deposit Confirmations Work in Swap Integrations
item.description: A swap service detects an XMR deposit through its wallet scan, matches it to an order, then waits for block confirmations before releasing the other asset.

item.title: Why a Token Approval Fails in a Self-Custody Wallet
item.description: A failed token approval usually leaves the contract’s spending allowance unchanged; check the network, transaction status, token balance and requested spender before retrying.

item.title: Claim fees or remove liquidity? The timing mechanics
item.description: Claiming fees leaves a pool position open, while removing liquidity closes or shrinks it; timing matters when exposure, gas cost or fee share changes.

item.title: How Blackhole Contributions Set a Token Pool’s First Depth
item.description: Blackhole Genesis Pools pair project tokens with community assets; their contributions shape opening pool depth, provided the launch threshold is met.

item.title: Reconcile the LP Burn Before Treasury Exit
item.description: Reconcile an LP burn by matching the pool share retired to the assets received, then tie every transfer, fee and balance change to the treasury’s exit record.

item.title: How to Lower the Cost of Frequent Base Trades
item.description: Frequent trades on Base cost more than the quoted swap fee: network gas, pool charges and price impact stack up, while batching and timing can reduce the drag.

item.title: Four tests for a split-routed cross-chain swap
item.description: A split-routed swap divides one cross-chain trade across several paths; compare net output, bridge steps, destination delivery and failure handling before signing.

item.title: Find the Exact Collateral Token a Vault Accepts
item.description: A vault accepts a specific token contract on a specific network, so verify the chain and address before depositing; a familiar ticker alone cannot identify it.

item.title: When Is Faster Swap Settlement Worth Paying For?
item.description: Faster swap settlement matters when it changes usable time, failure exposure or execution cost; compare finality, route design and fees before paying for it.

item.title: How to Check a Pending Chainflip Swap
item.description: A pending Chainflip swap can mean a deposit is unconfirmed, the trade is executing, or output is being sent; identify the stage and its chain record before acting.

item.title: How CLMM Ranges Shape Your Liquidity Position
item.description: A CLMM range sets where your liquidity can trade, shaping token exposure and fee earning; range width affects how often it stays active and needs attention.

item.title: Compare Bridge Routes by Pricing the Withdrawal Leg
item.description: A bridge quote is only comparable after you price destination gas, withdrawal steps and any final swap; compare the amount you can actually use.

item.title: Fund a First Purchase by Matching the Chain, Asset and Gas
item.description: Fund a first purchase on a new blockchain by matching the asset, network and gas token, then choosing a direct withdrawal, bridge or on-ramp that fits your route.

item.title: Why Mantle Bridge Deposits and Withdrawals Take Different Time
item.description: A Mantle deposit waits for Ethereum confirmation and delivery to the L2; a withdrawal adds a challenge period and a separate Ethereum claim, so plan time and gas.

item.title: What Happens When a Bridge Token Callback Fails
item.description: A callback can fail after a bridge transfer moves, leaving the destination action incomplete; recovery depends on message state and retry rules.

item.title: How BSC Swap Routes Work, and Which Ones Fail Less
item.description: A BSC swap route is more reliable when its pools, quote and execution limits agree; compare liquidity, hop count and minimum output before signing.

item.title: Three Checks Before You Trust a BSC Token Chart
item.description: A BSC token chart reflects trades in a specific liquidity pool; check the token address, pool depth and transaction history before treating its price as meaningful.

item.title: Three Signals That Show a Bridge Deposit Is Complete
item.description: A bridge deposit is complete only when the destination transaction succeeds and settles; source confirmation and a pending relay are earlier stages, not proof of delivery.

item.title: Why Polygon bridge transfers take different amounts of time
item.description: Polygon bridge time depends on direction: deposits wait for Ethereum confirmation and Polygon processing, while withdrawals add a validator checkpoint and an Ethereum claim.

item.title: Five Checks for Omnichain Routes as Networks Change
item.description: Routing depends on contracts, verifiers and execution rules lining up across chains; five checks help keep the path valid when networks or settings change.
